"'''Love's Theme'''" is an [[instrumental]] piece written by [[Barry White]] in 1965<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rubython |first=Tom |title=White Music - The Barry White Story |date=2017 |isbn=978-0-9934731-7-3}}</ref> but recorded and released as a single by White's [[The Love Unlimited Orchestra|Love Unlimited Orchestra]] in late 1973. It was one of the few instrumental and purely [[orchestra]]l singles to reach #1 on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]] chart in the United States, which it did in early 1974.<ref>{{cite book |title=  Joel Whitburn's Top Pop Singles, 14th Edition: 1955-2012 |last=Whitburn |first=Joel |authorlink=Joel Whitburn |year=2013 |publisher=Record Research |page=518}}</ref> ''Billboard'' ranked it as #3 on the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1974|Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1974]]. Over the years, "Love’s Theme" became one of the best-selling pop instrumentals of all time.

"Love's Theme" is an instrumental piece written by Barry White in 1965 but recorded and released as a single by White's Love Unlimited Orchestra in late 1973. It was one of the few instrumental and purely orchestral singles to reach #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in the United States, which it did in early 1974. Billboard ranked it as #3 on the Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1974. Over the years, "Love’s Theme" became one of the best-selling pop instrumentals of all time.

sections.heading: Background and release
sections.wikitext:
The song was included on two albums: 1973's ''[[Under the Influence of... Love Unlimited]]'' (by the vocal group [[Love Unlimited]]) and 1974's ''[[Rhapsody in White]]'' by the Love Unlimited Orchestra. Love Unlimited would re-release the song for their subsequent album, ''[[In Heat (Love Unlimited album)|In Heat]]'' (1974), only this time with different orchestral arrangements and lyrics written by [[Aaron Schroeder]].

The recording (with a large string orchestra, modified guitar and big rhythm section) is considered to be an influence on the [[disco]] sound, which would increase in popularity the following year. The song was also popular on the [[Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks|Adult Contemporary]] chart in the United States, spending two weeks at #1, and was also a #1 on the [[Cashbox (magazine)|''Cash Box'']] chart. For several years, a shortened version of the original instrumental release was used in the opening sequence of the television golf ''[[PGA Tour on ABC]]'' broadcasting program.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nine Girls And A Guy |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2002/11/jennifer-lopez-200211 |website=Vanity Fair |date=November 2002}}</ref>

In [[Canada]], the single was similarly successful, being a #1 on the ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM 100]]'' National Singles Chart on March 2, 1974.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/rpm/028020-119.01-e.php?brws_s=1&file_num=nlc008388.4986a&type=1&interval=24&PHPSESSID=ccntousk30frf6h4jsn237nm12|title=Item Display – RPM – Library and Archives Canada|work=collectionscanada.gc.ca|access-date=2011-07-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023192851/http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/rpm/028020-119.01-e.php?brws_s=1&file_num=nlc008388.4986a&type=1&interval=24&PHPSESSID=ccntousk30frf6h4jsn237nm12|archive-date=2012-10-23|url-status=dead}}</ref> "Love's Theme" was sampled by the Italian group [[Black Box (band)|Black Box]] in their 1989 song "[[Ride on Time]]".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=2019-05-08 |title=The Number Ones: The Love Unlimited Orchestra's "Love's Theme" |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2042808/the-number-ones-the-love-unlimited-orchestras-loves-theme/columns/the-number-ones/ |access-date=2023-04-13 |website=[[Stereogum]] |language=en}}</ref>
sections.text:
The song was included on two albums: 1973's Under the Influence of... Love Unlimited (by the vocal group Love Unlimited) and 1974's Rhapsody in White by the Love Unlimited Orchestra. Love Unlimited would re-release the song for their subsequent album, In Heat (1974), only this time with different orchestral arrangements and lyrics written by Aaron Schroeder.

The recording (with a large string orchestra, modified guitar and big rhythm section) is considered to be an influence on the disco sound, which would increase in popularity the following year. The song was also popular on the Adult Contemporary chart in the United States, spending two weeks at #1, and was also a #1 on the Cash Box chart. For several years, a shortened version of the original instrumental release was used in the opening sequence of the television golf PGA Tour on ABC broadcasting program.

In Canada, the single was similarly successful, being a #1 on the RPM 100 National Singles Chart on March 2, 1974. "Love's Theme" was sampled by the Italian group Black Box in their 1989 song "Ride on Time".

sections.heading: Legacy
sections.wikitext:
In 1975–76, [[WPIX|WPIX-TV]] in New York would end its 10:00pm broadcast of ''Harper News'' (later ''[[Action News]]'') with "Love's Theme".<ref>{{Citation |title=Action News close with the Harpers, followed by Editorial Feedback, 7/10/75 | date=12 March 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FW0ci4AI7XM |access-date=2023-06-27 |language=en}}</ref> It was also used as the boarding music for [[Cathay Pacific]] during the 1980s<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Cobaj |date=22 May 2019 |title=6 Hongkongers share 'what Cathay means to me' |url=https://www.cathaypacific.com/cx/en_US/inspiration/cathay-stories/what-cathay-means-to-me.html}}</ref> and as the theme song of the Brazilian soap opera ''[[Celebridade]]''.

Since 2000, it has been the theme song for the Italian talk show ''[[:it:C'è posta per te (programma televisivo)|C'è posta per te]]'', on air on [[Canale 5]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.corriere.it/spettacoli/cards/c-posta-te-riparte-alberto-sordi-primo-ospite-citazioni-cinematografiche-7-segreti/chi-accompagna-storie-c-posta-te-la-sua-musica.shtml|title=C’è posta per te riparte: la lite tra Cassano e Totti, lo svenimento in studio, sette momenti davvero cult|first=Arianna|last=Ascione|date=January 13, 2024|website=Corriere della Sera}}</ref> The 2024 [[PBS]] series ''Disco: Soundtrack of a Revolution'' explores the importance of "Love's Theme" to the history of disco music.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pbs.org/video/rock-the-boat-nxxaev/ | title=Disco: Soundtrack of a Revolution | Rock the Boat | Episode 1 | website=[[PBS]] }}</ref>
sections.text:
In 1975–76, WPIX-TV in New York would end its 10:00pm broadcast of Harper News (later Action News) with "Love's Theme". It was also used as the boarding music for Cathay Pacific during the 1980s and as the theme song of the Brazilian soap opera Celebridade.

Since 2000, it has been the theme song for the Italian talk show C'è posta per te, on air on Canale 5. The 2024 PBS series Disco: Soundtrack of a Revolution explores the importance of "Love's Theme" to the history of disco music.
